Power System Models

Power system component model definitions and implementations.

Overview

Powerful.jl includes models for:

  • AC Buses - Voltage and angle reference points
  • Static Models - PQ loads, PV generators, Slack buses
  • Branches - Transmission lines and transformers
  • Shunts - Fixed and switchable shunts
  • Dynamic Models - GENCLS, GENROU, GENSAL, ESST1A, etc.
  • Topological Elements - Areas, zones, owners

All Component Models

Powerful.Models.AreaInterchange — Type
struct AreaInterchange{Tv} <: AbstractModel

Area interchange data records.

Fields

  • i::Int16: Area number (1 through the maximum number of areas at the current size level)
  • isw::Int32: Area slack bus number for interchange control, given by its bus number or extended bus name enclosed in single quotes. The bus must be a generator (type two) bus in the specified area. Any area containing a system swing bus (type three) must have either that swing bus or a bus number of zero specified for its area slack bus number. isw = 0 by default.
  • pdes::Any: Desired net interchange leaving the area (export) in MW.
  • ptol::Any: Interchange tolerance bandwidth; entered in MW. ptol = 10.0 by default.
  • arname::InlineStrings.String15: Alphanumeric identifier assigned to area I. The name may contain up to twelve characters. arname is set to twelve blanks by default.

Powerful.Models.Branch — Type
struct Branch{Tv} <: AbstractModel

In PSS/E and similar tools, the basic transmission line model is an Equivalent Pi model connected between network buses.

Data for shunt equipment units, such as reactors, which are connected to and switched with the line, are entered in the same data record.

!!! note "Transformers" Branches to be modeled as transformers are not specified in this data category; # rather, they are specified in the

Fields

  • i::Int32: Branch from bus number

  • j::Int32: Branch to bus number. Negative value designates it as the metered end

  • ckt::InlineStrings.String3: One- or two-character branch circuit identifier. Default is '1'

  • r::Any: Branch resistance in pu
  • x::Any: Branch reactance in pu Must be nonzero
  • b::Any: Total branch charging susceptance in pu
  • rate_a::Any: First loading rating in MVA. Zero means branch excluded from loading examination
  • rate_b::Any: Second loading rating in MVA
  • rate_c::Any: Third loading rating in MVA
  • gi::Any: Real part of line shunt admittance at bus i end in pu
  • bi::Any: Imaginary part of line shunt admittance at bus i end in pu
  • gj::Any: Real part of line shunt admittance at bus j end in pu
  • bj::Any: Imaginary part of line shunt admittance at bus j end in pu
  • st::Bool: Branch status 1=in-service, 0=out-of-service
  • met::Int8: Metering end indicator
  • len::Any: Line length in user-selected units
  • o1::Int16: First owner number
  • f1::Any: Fraction of total ownership for first owner
  • o2::Union{Missing, Int16}: Second owner number
  • f2::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Fraction of total ownership for second owner
  • o3::Union{Missing, Int16}: Third owner number
  • f3::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Fraction of total ownership for third owner
  • o4::Union{Missing, Int16}: Fourth owner number
  • f4::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Fraction of total ownership for fourth owner

Powerful.Models.Bus — Type
mutable struct Bus{Tv} <: AbstractModel

Network bus data records.

Fields

  • i::Int32: Bus number (1 to 999997).

  • name::InlineStrings.String15: Alphanumeric identifier assigned to bus 'I'.

    The name may be up to twelve characters and must be enclosed in single quotes. NAME may contain any combination of blanks, uppercase letters, numbers and special characters, but the first character must not be a minus sign.

  • basekv::Any: Bus base voltage in kV.

  • ide::Int8: Bus type code:

    • 1 - load bus or other bus without any generator boundary condition.
    • 2 - generator or plant bus either regulating voltage or with a fixed reactive power (Mvar). A generator that reaches its reactive power limit will no longer control voltage but rather hold reactive power at its limit.
    • 3 - swing bus or slack bus. It has no power or reactive limits and regulates voltage at a fixed reference angle.
    • 4 - disconnected or isolated bus.

  • area::Int16: Area number. 1 through the maximum number of areas at the current size level.

  • zone::Int16: Zone number. 1 through the maximum number of zones at the current size level.

  • owner::Int16: Owner number. 1 through the maximum number of owners at the current size level.

  • vm::Any: Bus voltage magnitude in pu.

  • va::Any: Bus voltage angle in degrees.

  • nvhi::Any: Normal voltage magnitude high limit in pu.

  • nvlo::Any: Normal voltage magnitude low limit in pu.

  • evhi::Any: Emergency voltage magnitude high limit in pu.

  • evlo::Any: Emergency voltage magnitude low limit in pu.

source

struct Owner <: AbstractModel

PSS/E allows users to identify ownership of facilities, equipment, and loads through owner assignments. Major network elements can have up to four different owners, enabling interpretation and reporting of results based on ownership.

  • owname::InlineStrings.String15: Alphanumeric identifier assigned to owner i. The name may contain up to twelve characters and must be enclosed in single quotes. Can contain any combination of blanks, uppercase letters, numbers and special characters. Set to twelve blanks by default.

Powerful.Models.PV — Type
mutable struct PV{Tv} <: AbstractModel

PV generator data records.

Fields

  • i::Int32: Bus number or extended bus name enclosed in single quotes

  • id::InlineStrings.String3: One or two character uppercase non-blank alphanumeric machine identifier. Used to distinguish multiple machines at bus i. Recommended to use '1' for buses with single machine.

  • pg::Any: Generator active power output in MW. Default: 0.0

  • qg::Any: Generator reactive power output in Mvar. Only needed if case is to be treated as solved. Default: 0.0

  • qt::Any: Maximum generator reactive power output in Mvar. Must equal fixed Mvar output for non-regulating generators. Default: 9999.0
  • qb::Any: Minimum generator reactive power output in Mvar. Must equal fixed Mvar output for non-regulating generators. Default: -9999.0

  • vs::Any: Regulated voltage setpoint in per unit. Default: 1.0

  • ireg::Int32: Remote bus number to regulate voltage. Must be type 1 or 2 bus. Zero means generator regulates own voltage. Must be zero for type 3 (swing) bus. Default: 0

  • mbase::Any: Total MVA base of units represented by this machine. Required for switching studies, fault analysis and dynamic simulation. Default: system base MVA
  • zr::Any: Real part of machine impedance ZSORCE in pu on MBASE. Used for switching studies, fault analysis and dynamic simulation. For dynamics: set to unsaturated subtransient/transient impedance. For short-circuit: use saturated values. Default: 0.0

  • zx::Any: Imaginary part of machine impedance ZSORCE. See zr. Default: 1.0

  • rt::Any: Real part of step-up transformer impedance in pu on MBASE. Set to zero if transformer explicitly modeled. Default: 0.0

  • xt::Any: Imaginary part of step-up transformer impedance. See rt. Default: 0.0

  • gtap::Any: Step-up transformer off-nominal turns ratio in pu. Only used if transformer impedance nonzero. Default: 1.0

  • stat::Bool: Machine status: 1 for in-service, 0 for out-of-service. Default: 1
  • rmpct::Any: Percent of total Mvar for voltage control at regulated bus. Required if multiple devices control voltage at bus IREG. Must be positive. Default: 100.0

  • pt::Any: Maximum generator active power output in MW. Default: 9999.0

  • pb::Any: Minimum generator active power output in MW. Default: -9999.0

  • o1::Int16: Primary owner number (1 to max owners). Default: owner of bus i

  • f1::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Fraction of ownership for owner 1 (>0). Normalized to sum to 1.0. Default: 1.0

  • o2::Union{Missing, Int16}: Second owner number. Default: 0

  • f2::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 2. See f1

  • o3::Union{Missing, Int16}: Third owner number. Default: 0

  • f3::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 3. See f1

  • o4::Union{Missing, Int16}: Fourth owner number. Default: 0

  • f4::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 4. See f1

  • wmod::Union{Missing, Int8}: Wind machine control mode: 0 = not wind machine 1 = wind machine with QT/QB limits 2 = wind machine with limits from output and wpf 3 = fixed reactive power from output and wpf Default: 0

  • wpf::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Power factor for reactive power calculation when wmod is 2 or 3. Sign determines reactive power direction. Default: 1.0

Powerful.Models.Shunt — Type
mutable struct Shunt{Tv} <: AbstractModel

Fixed shunt compensator data records.

Fixed shunts are voltage-dependent reactive power devices used for voltage support and reactive power compensation in power systems. They typically represent:

  • Capacitor banks (negative BL, provides reactive support)
  • Shunt reactors (positive BL, absorbs reactive power)

Fields

  • i::Int32: Bus number or extended bus name enclosed in single quotes

  • id::InlineStrings.String3: One- or two-character uppercase non-blank alphanumeric shunt identifier. Used to distinguish multiple shunts at bus i. Recommended to use '1' for single shunt.

  • status::Int8: Shunt status: 1 for in-service, 0 for out-of-service

  • gl::Any: Active component of shunt admittance in MW at 1.0 pu voltage. Typically zero for fixed shunts. Positive = resistive load.

  • bl::Any: Reactive component of shunt admittance in Mvar at 1.0 pu voltage. PSS/E convention: Positive = capacitive (provides reactive support) Negative = inductive (absorbs reactive power)
source
Powerful.Models.Slack — Type
mutable struct Slack{Tv} <: AbstractModel

Slack (swing/reference) bus generator data records.

Slack buses provide the voltage and angle reference for the power system. They share the same data structure as PV generators but have different equation semantics:

  • PV: Power injection + voltage control
  • Slack: Angle reference + voltage reference

Fields

  • i::Int32: Bus number or extended bus name enclosed in single quotes

  • id::InlineStrings.String3: One or two character uppercase non-blank alphanumeric machine identifier. Used to distinguish multiple machines at bus i. Recommended to use '1' for buses with single machine.

  • pg::Any: Generator active power output in MW (measured, not setpoint). Default: 0.0

  • qg::Any: Generator reactive power output in Mvar (measured, not setpoint). Only needed if case is to be treated as solved. Default: 0.0

  • qt::Any: Maximum generator reactive power output in Mvar. Must equal fixed Mvar output for non-regulating generators. Default: 9999.0
  • qb::Any: Minimum generator reactive power output in Mvar. Must equal fixed Mvar output for non-regulating generators. Default: -9999.0

  • vs::Any: Regulated voltage setpoint in per unit. Default: 1.0

  • ireg::Int32: Remote bus number to regulate voltage. Must be type 1 or 2 bus. Zero means generator regulates own voltage. Must be zero for type 3 (swing) bus. Default: 0

  • mbase::Any: Total MVA base of units represented by this machine. Required for switching studies, fault analysis and dynamic simulation. Default: system base MVA
  • zr::Any: Real part of machine impedance ZSORCE in pu on MBASE. Used for switching studies, fault analysis and dynamic simulation. For dynamics: set to unsaturated subtransient/transient impedance. For short-circuit: use saturated values. Default: 0.0

  • zx::Any: Imaginary part of machine impedance ZSORCE. See zr. Default: 1.0

  • rt::Any: Real part of step-up transformer impedance in pu on MBASE. Set to zero if transformer explicitly modeled. Default: 0.0

  • xt::Any: Imaginary part of step-up transformer impedance. See rt. Default: 0.0

  • gtap::Any: Step-up transformer off-nominal turns ratio in pu. Only used if transformer impedance nonzero. Default: 1.0

  • stat::Bool: Machine status: 1 for in-service, 0 for out-of-service. Default: 1
  • rmpct::Any: Percent of total Mvar for voltage control at regulated bus. Required if multiple devices control voltage at bus IREG. Must be positive. Default: 100.0

  • pt::Any: Maximum generator active power output in MW. Default: 9999.0

  • pb::Any: Minimum generator active power output in MW. Default: -9999.0

  • o1::Int16: Primary owner number (1 to max owners). Default: owner of bus i

  • f1::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Fraction of ownership for owner 1 (>0). Normalized to sum to 1.0. Default: 1.0

  • o2::Union{Missing, Int16}: Second owner number. Default: 0

  • f2::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 2. See f1

  • o3::Union{Missing, Int16}: Third owner number. Default: 0

  • f3::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 3. See f1

  • o4::Union{Missing, Int16}: Fourth owner number. Default: 0

  • f4::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Ownership fraction for owner 4. See f1

  • wmod::Union{Missing, Int8}: Wind machine control mode: 0 = not wind machine 1 = wind machine with QT/QB limits 2 = wind machine with limits from output and wpf 3 = fixed reactive power from output and wpf Default: 0

  • wpf::Union{Missing, Tv} where Tv: Power factor for reactive power calculation when wmod is 2 or 3. Sign determines reactive power direction. Default: 1.0

Powerful.Models.Transformer3W — Type
struct Transformer3W{Tv} <: AbstractModel

This struct represents a three-winding transformer as parsed from PSS/E data. It is a transient data structure that gets converted to three 2-winding transformers with a virtual bus in a star configuration.

Note: This struct does not define residuals - it's only used for parsing and conversion. Power flow computations use the equivalent 2W transformers.

Powerful.Models.Zone — Type
struct Zone <: AbstractModel

All buses and loads can be assigned to reside in a zone of the network. Zones enable users to develop reports and check results on a zonal basis, allowing highly specific reporting and interpretation of analytical results. Zone assignments are made by specifying zone numbers in the data records for buses and loads.

Fields

  • i::Int16: Zone number (1 through the maximum number of zones at the current size level)

  • zoname::InlineStrings.String15: Alphanumeric identifier assigned to zone i. The name may contain up to twelve characters and must be enclosed in single quotes. Can contain any combination of blanks, uppercase letters, numbers and special characters. Set to twelve blanks by default.

source
Powerful.Models.all_models — Method
all_models()

Get all registered model types.

Convenience accessor for MODEL_REGISTRY[].models. This is the recommended way to access all registered models instead of directly accessing the registry.

Returns

  • Tuple of all registered model types

Example

# Get all models
models = all_models()

# Use in load_models
models_data = load_models(case, all_models())

# Use in SystemModel (though default already uses all models)
sys = SystemModel(case, all_models())

# Or just use the default which does this automatically:
sys = SystemModel(case)  # Uses all_models() by default

See Also

  • MODEL_REGISTRY: The underlying registry
  • get_registered_models: Lower-level accessor
source
Powerful.Models.convert_3w_to_star! — Method
convert_3w_to_star!(models::NamedTuple, sbase_system::Float64) -> (NamedTuple, Union{Nothing, Dict})

Convert 3-winding transformers to star configuration with virtual buses.

This function:

  1. Creates virtual buses for each 3W transformer
  2. Converts delta impedances to star impedances (properly handling CZ/CM codes)
  3. Creates three 2W transformers for each 3W transformer
  4. Removes Transformer3W from models tuple
  5. Returns metadata for tracking virtual buses

Arguments

  • models: NamedTuple of model vectors (must include Transformer3W if present)
  • sbase_system: System MVA base (for impedance conversions)

Returns

  • (models_new, metadata): New models tuple without Transformer3W, and conversion metadata dictionary

Metadata Dictionary Keys

  • "original_buses": Vector{Tuple{Int32, Int32, Int32}} - Original 3W transformer buses (i, j, k)
  • "virtual_buses": Vector{Int32} - Virtual bus numbers created
  • "circuit_ids": Vector{String} - Circuit IDs of original 3W transformers
source
Powerful.Models.get_controlled_group — Method
get_controlled_group(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Union{Symbol, Nothing}

Declare which initialization group this controller model links to.

Controllers (governors, exciters, PSS) link to models in another group (typically :generators) by matching (BUS, ID) keys. This is different from get_replacement_map which is for models that REPLACE other models.

Returns:

  • nothing (default) - Model doesn't control other models (e.g., GENCLS)
  • :generators - Model controls generators (e.g., TGOV1, EXST1, PSS)

Example

get_controlled_group(::Type{<:TGOV1}) = :generators  # Links to GENCLS/GENROU
get_controlled_group(::Type{<:EXST1}) = :generators  # Links to GENCLS/GENROU

Usage

The DYR parser uses this trait to:

  1. Identify controller models that need two-phase parsing
  2. Find target models in the specified group for (BUS, ID) matching

See Also

  • get_initialization_group: Declares which group this model belongs to
  • get_replacement_map: For models that replace other models
source

get_data_inheritance(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Dict{Symbol, Dict{Symbol, Symbol}}

Return a dictionary specifying which data to inherit from linked models.

This trait declares which fields should be copied from power flow models during dynamic model construction (e.g., inheriting reactance values).

Returns Dict{Symbol, Dict{Symbol, Symbol}} where:

  • Outer keys are target model symbols (:PV, :Slack)
  • Inner dicts map: destination field => source field

Default: Empty dictionary (no data inheritance)

Example

function get_data_inheritance(::Type{<:GENCLS})
    Dict(
        :PV => Dict(:xd_p => :zx),      # Copy PV.zx → GENCLS.xd_p
        :Slack => Dict(:xd_p => :zx),   # Copy Slack.zx → GENCLS.xd_p
    )
end

This declares that when linking to PV or Slack, copy their zx field to GENCLS's xd_p field.

Notes

  • Used by parse_gencls() to inherit power flow data
  • Separate from getreplacementmap to avoid mixing concerns
source
Powerful.Models.get_dyr_model_name — Method
get_dyr_model_name(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Union{String, Nothing}

Return the DYR model name for this type, or nothing if not a DYR model.

Dynamic models that can be parsed from PSSE DYR files override this to return their DYR model name string (e.g., "GENCLS", "GENROU", "EXST1", etc.).

Default: nothing (not a DYR-parseable model)

Implementation

DYR models override this to declare their model name:

get_dyr_model_name(::Type{<:GENCLS}) = "GENCLS"
get_dyr_model_name(::Type{<:GENROU}) = "GENROU"
get_dyr_model_name(::Type{<:EXST1}) = "EXST1"

Usage

The DYR parser (parse_dyr) uses this trait to:

  1. Automatically discover which models can be parsed from DYR files
  2. Map DYR model names (strings from PowerDynData) to Julia types
  3. Enable generic parsing without hardcoded model names

Example

# Parser iterates over all registered models
for model_type in all_models()
    dyr_name = get_dyr_model_name(model_type)
    if !isnothing(dyr_name) && haskey(dyn_data.models, dyr_name)
        # Parse this model type from DYR data
        params = parse_dynamic_model(model_type, dyn_data.models[dyr_name].data, ...)
    end
end

See Also

  • parse_dynamic_model: Implements DYR parsing logic for each model
  • all_models: Returns all registered model types
  • is_dynamic_model: Determines if model participates in TDS
source
Powerful.Models.get_foreign_keys — Method
get_foreign_keys(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Dict{Symbol, Symbol}

Return a dictionary mapping field names to model types they reference.

This trait declares which fields in the model are foreign keys that need external ID → internal index conversion during linking.

Returns Dict{Symbol, Symbol} where:

  • Keys are field names (e.g., :BUS)
  • Values are model type symbols they reference (e.g., :Bus)

Default: Empty dictionary (no foreign keys)

Example

function get_foreign_keys(::Type{<:GENCLS})
    Dict(:BUS => :Bus)  # BUS field references Bus model
end

This declares that the BUS field contains external bus numbers that must be converted to internal Bus indices during linking.

Notes

  • Used by DYR parser to handle external→internal ID conversion
  • Separate from getreplacementmap (which specifies replacement targets)
source

Powerful.Models.get_replacement_map — Method
get_replacement_map(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}

Return a dictionary mapping static model symbols to field correspondence.

This trait declares which static power flow models the dynamic model can replace and how to link instances between DYR data (external IDs) and power flow data.

Returns Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple} where:

  • Keys are model type symbols (:PV, :Slack, etc.)
  • Values are NamedTuple(source_fields=(...), target_fields=(...))

Default: Empty dictionary (model doesn't replace anything)

Usage

The linking system uses this to:

  1. Identify which PV/Slack generators to filter out
  2. Match dynamic model instances (by external ID) to static instances
  3. Extract initialization data (P, Q, V setpoints)

Example

function get_replacement_map(::Type{<:GENCLS})
    return Dict(
        :PV => (source_fields=(:i, :id), target_fields=(:i, :id)),
        :Slack => (source_fields=(:i, :id), target_fields=(:i, :id)),
    )
end

This declares that GENCLS replaces both PV and Slack generators, matching by bus number i and machine ID id.

Notes

  • Uses symbols (:PV) not types to avoid circular dependencies
  • Linking system resolves symbols at runtime
  • Field names must match struct field names in both models
source
Powerful.Models.is_dynamic_model — Method
is_dynamic_model(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Bool

Return true if the model participates in time-domain simulation.

Dynamic models are included in TDS systems. This includes:

  • Models with differential states (GENCLS, GENROU, etc.)
  • Models that enforce algebraic constraints in TDS (Slack - enforces voltage/angle)

Default: false for all models (static power flow only)

Implementation

Dynamic models override this to return true:

is_dynamic_model(::Type{<:GENCLS}) = true  # Has differential states
is_dynamic_model(::Type{<:Slack}) = true   # Enforces algebraic constraints
source
Powerful.Models.parse_dynamic_model — Method
parse_dynamic_model(
    ::Type{M},
    dyr_data,
    sys_pf::SystemModel,
    links::ModelLinks
) where M -> StructArray{M}

Parse dynamic model parameters from DYR data with linking to power flow models.

This is a trait function for dynamic models that need to:

  1. Parse parameters from DYR files
  2. Link to static power flow models (PV, Slack)
  3. Inherit data from linked models (e.g., reactance values)

This is separate from parse_model because DYR parsing requires linking context that static RAW parsing doesn't need.

Arguments

  • M::Type{<:AbstractModel} - Dynamic model type (e.g., GENCLS, GENROU)
  • dyr_data - Raw DYR data (typically StructVector from PowerDynData)
  • sys_pf::SystemModel - Power flow system (for data inheritance)
  • links::ModelLinks - Instance mappings between DYR and power flow models

Returns

StructArray{M} with all model parameters filled

Implementation

Dynamic models override this for their specific DYR parsing logic:

function parse_dynamic_model(
    ::Type{GENCLS},
    dyr_data::StructVector,
    sys_pf::SystemModel,
    links::ModelLinks
)
    # Extract DYR parameters, inherit PF data, construct instances
    # Returns StructArray{GENCLS}
end

Default

Throws error for models that don't implement DYR parsing.

See Also

  • parse_model: For static RAW file parsing
  • get_data_inheritance: Declares which fields to inherit
  • get_replacement_map: Declares which models to replace
source
Powerful.Models.post_process_models — Method
post_process_models(raw_data, models::NamedTuple, model_types, system_base::Float64) -> NamedTuple

Apply all post-processing transformations to parsed models.

This is the single entry point for Formats module to call. It coordinates individual post-processors based on which model types were requested.

Arguments

  • raw_data: PowerFlowData.Network (needed for 3W transformer parsing)
  • models: NamedTuple of parsed models from load_models
  • model_types: Requested model types (to determine which processors to run)
  • system_base: System MVA base (for 3W conversion)

Returns

NamedTuple with all transformations applied

Powerful.Foundation.model_metadata — Function
model_metadata(::Type{M}) where {M<:AbstractModel}

Get metadata for a model type. All models must implement this method.

The metadata describes the model's variables (both internal and external), residual equations, and output variables.

Arguments

  • Model type (e.g., PQ, Bus, Branch)

Returns

  • ModelMetadata object describing the model's structure

Example

# Get metadata for PQ load model
metadata = model_metadata(PQ)

# Access metadata properties
metadata.vars      # Vector of ModelVar
metadata.residuals # Vector of ModelResidual

Implementation

Each model must define this method in its source file:

function model_metadata(::Type{MyModel})
    ModelMetadata(
        name = :MyModel,
        vars = [...],
        output_vars = [...],
        residuals = [...]
    )
end
source
model_metadata(model_vec::AbstractModel)

Convenience method to get metadata from a model vector instance.

Arguments

  • model_vec: Model vector instance (e.g., PQVec, BusVec)

Returns

  • ModelMetadata for the base model type

Example

pq_vec = parse_model(PQ, case)

# Old way
metadata = model_metadata(PQ)

# New way (more convenient)
metadata = model_metadata(pq_vec)
source
